title: Line regulation: untrimmed output shift across the full 3.3 V +/-10% supply range
claim: README.md 'Target specification (ratified -- see DR-005, issue #1)' row 'Supply' (3.3 V +/-10%) read as an output-shift requirement, checked against the only bound the ratified spec implies without inventing a number: the supply-induced shift must fit inside the entire +/-2% untrimmed output-accuracy window (48 mV p-p on 1.20 V). NECESSARY, not sufficient -- a real budget gives line regulation a fraction of that window. Setting a dedicated line-regulation line item remains a future spec pass's call; these numbers are its input.

analyses: meas dc vrefnom FIND v(vref) AT=3.3

measurements.name: line_shift_mv
measurements.note: Peak-to-peak VREF excursion across 2.97..3.63 V. Limit is DR-005's full +/-2% untrimmed output-accuracy window (48 mV on 1.20 V) -- see the claim: necessary, not sufficient, and not a dedicated line-regulation spec number. Meaningful only at the tightened solver tolerances set in deck.options; at ngspice's defaults this measurement is a readout of the solver's convergence noise floor rather than of the circuit.

measurements.name: line_reg_pct_per_v
measurements.note: Informational (no limit): the same excursion expressed as a fractional output change per volt of supply, normalized to VREF at the nominal 3.30 V. The conventional way to quote line regulation.

measurements.name: line_psrr_db
measurements.note: Informational (no limit): large-signal DC supply rejection, 20*log10(dVDD/dVREF) over the full 2.97..3.63 V range. This is the independent counterpart of sim/psrr-dc/'s small-signal 0.1 Hz psrr_dc. The two are not the same quantity -- this one is an average slope over 0.66 V of supply while psrr_dc is the local slope at one bias point -- so on a characteristic with a shallow interior minimum they are expected to differ by a few dB, with this one the conservative (lower) figure. What they must NOT do is differ by tens of dB: that is what the first run of this bench did (54 dB here against 93 dB there at tt / 125 degC / 3.30 V), and the cause was the solver's convergence noise floor swamping the real shift, not a disagreement about the circuit. See the tolerance note below.

measurements.name: vref_nom
measurements.note: VREF at the nominal 3.30 V supply. Loose +/-5% sanity band only -- the +/-2% output-accuracy claim belongs to sim/output-voltage-tc/, not to this bench. Here it is the normalization reference and a check that the core was actually regulating during the sweep.

measurements.name: sweep_start_v
measurements.note: Guard: asserts the in-deck supply sweep really started at 2.97 V (-10%).

measurements.name: sweep_end_v
measurements.note: Guard: asserts the in-deck supply sweep really ended at 3.63 V (+10%).

measurements.name: n_supply_points
measurements.note: Guard: asserts the supply sweep produced the expected 31 points. If it silently collapsed to a single operating point, line_shift_mv would read 0 mV and look like a perfect pass.

spread_checks.note: Primary corner-liveness guard for this bench: VREF at the nominal supply must move by at least 5 mV across the 15-point process/temperature matrix. It spans ~33 mV (1.1747 V at the hot corners to 1.2082 V at the cold ones), so this is a wide-margin assertion that the .lib corner include and .temp really are reaching the simulator. It is placed on VREF rather than on the line shift because VREF is the quantity with a large, well-understood corner dependence; the line shift is a second-order effect measured in tens of microvolts and is a poor liveness signal.

Secondary guard: the supply-induced shift must itself move by at least 5 uV across the matrix. RE-SCALED from the original 0.05 mV. That threshold was set against the first run of this bench, whose 0.11 .. 1.27 mV readings turned out to be the DC solver's convergence noise floor rather than the circuit (see the tolerance note below). With the noise removed the real quantity is 0.0074 .. 0.030 mV, so a 0.05 mV spread requirement can never be met and the guard fires on every run -- as it did on record 20260803-115354-7759435, which is committed as a failing record. The new threshold is scaled to the resolved magnitude and still leaves ~4.5x margin on the observed 0.023 mV spread, while sitting three orders of magnitude above the noise floor at these tolerances. Note what did NOT change: the pass window on the measurement itself (24 mV) is untouched -- no spec bound was moved to make anything pass, only a harness self-check that had been calibrated against a number now known to be an artifact.

notes: Supply is swept INSIDE the deck because the claim is about the shift across a range, not about any single supply point; the runner is therefore invoked with --supply 3.3 --subset-reason. Process and temperature run in full (5 x 3 = 15 points).
The corner axes above declare the full PVT matrix so the manifest stays the canonical statement of what the claim requires and the subset is visible as a subset in the record.

Solver tolerances are tightened well past ngspice's defaults: reltol=1e-6 (default 1e-3), vntol=1e-9 (default 1e-6), abstol=1e-15 (default 1e-12). This is a MEASUREMENT-RESOLUTION requirement, not a taste preference. At the default reltol=1e-3 the DC solver is only obliged to converge a ~1.175 V node to ~1.2 mV, and the first run of sim/line-regulation/ (record 20260803-100723-77b96e3) duly reported a 0.11 .. 1.27 mV supply-induced output shift that, on inspection of the raw sweep, was non-monotonic point-to-point jitter at exactly that amplitude -- i.e. the solver's convergence noise floor, not a property of the circuit. Re-run with these tolerances the same sweep is smooth and monotone with a shallow minimum near 3.45 V, and the shift drops to tens of microvolts. Every DC-based bench in this suite shares the setting so that all four are read off the same, resolved operating point.
